questions.prompt: G = 5, c = 0.2, gamma = 0.9. Smallest repeatable bonus for which the 2-cycle loop beats finishing? (three decimals)
With a repeatable bonus of 2 and G = 10, c = 0.1, lowering gamma from 0.95 to 0.8 will
options: remove the loophole, because the threshold bonus rises and 2 falls below it
create the loophole, because every reward is then smaller
change nothing, since the repeatable bonus is fixed at 2
make finishing impossible, since the horizon becomes too short
questions.explanation: b* = 10(1-0.64)+0.1*1.8 = 3.78 > 2, so finishing wins at gamma = 0.8.

questions.prompt: Shaping with F = phi(s') - phi(s) without gamma, phi(s) = -(5-s), loop 2->3->2->3... with gamma = 0.9. Discounted sum of F per loop start? (three decimals)
Which evaluation is most informative about whether a learned policy actually does the task?
options: Success rate and side-effect metrics computed from the world state on held-out episodes
The entropy of the policy, averaged over the states visited in the training episodes
The critic's value estimate at the start state, averaged over the training episodes
The average training return, reported over the last iterations of the training run
questions.explanation: Only task-level and state-derived metrics can detect a policy that exploits the training reward.

questions.prompt: phi(s) = -(8 - s), gamma = 1. For a terminating path starting at s = 2, by how much does the shaped return differ from the true return? (one decimal)
A bonus is paid only the first time the checkpoint is entered in an episode. Compared with a repeatable bonus, this
options: makes the problem non-Markov and therefore unsolvable by any reinforcement learner
removes the farming loop but requires the state to include whether the bonus was collected
is equivalent to a potential difference between the two states, so nothing changes
still allows farming through episode resets and repeated entries into the checkpoint
questions.explanation: A flag in the state restores the Markov property and closes the loop.

questions.prompt: You want to speed up learning on a sparse-reward arm task without changing which policy is optimal. Which addition is safe?
options: gamma*phi(s') - phi(s) with phi = minus the distance from gripper to object
a bonus proportional to the end-effector speed, to encourage fast reaching
+1 every time the gripper touches the object, to guide the arm toward it
+0.1 per step to encourage the arm to stay alive until it succeeds
questions.explanation: Only the potential difference is guaranteed to preserve the optimal policy; touch, living and speed bonuses can be farmed.
